chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote to Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام: “Is the testimony of the executor for the deceased concerning a debt owed to him by a man accepted along with another just witness?” So he عليه السلام signed: “If another just witness testifies with him, then an oath is upon the claimant.”

And he wrote to him: “Is it permissible for the executor to testify for the heir of the deceased, whether young or old, regarding a right belonging to him against the deceased or against someone else, while he is the receiver on behalf of the young heir, but there is no receiver for the adult?” So he عليه السلام signed: “Yes. The executor ought to testify with the truth and not conceal his testimony.”
And he wrote to him: “And is the testimony of the executor against the deceased concerning a debt accepted along with another just witness?” So he عليه السلام signed: “Yes, after an oath.”

key_terms.الْمَيِّتِ: the deceased person whose estate or liabilities are under discussion
key_terms.الْمُدَّعِي: the claimant who asserts the legal right
key_terms.الْوَصِيِّ: the executor or legatee entrusted with carrying out the affairs of the deceased
key_terms.بِدَيْنٍ: concerning a debt owed or claimed
key_terms.شَاهِدٍ: a witness whose testimony supports the legal claim
key_terms.شَهَادَةُ: legal testimony given in support of a claim
key_terms.عَدْلٍ: just and upright, qualifying the witness as legally reliable
key_terms.يَمِينٌ: an oath required to complete or support the claim

ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of an executor accepted in debt and inheritance cases in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith records legal responses from Imam al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام regarding the testimony of an executor in cases involving the deceased, heirs, and debts. It establishes that such testimony may be accepted with an additional just witness, and in certain cases with an accompanying oath. It also stresses that the executor should testify truthfully and not conceal testimony.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3362 - Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, may Allah (swt) have mercy on him, wrote to Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ali (as):
"Is the testimony of the executor (al-wasi) for the deceased regarding a debt owed to him by a man acceptable along with another just witness?"
Imam (as) replied: "If another just witness testifies with him, then the claimant must take an oath."

He also wrote to Imam (as): "Is it permissible for the executor to testify for the heir of the deceased, whether young or old, regarding a right owed to him by the deceased or by another person, especially if he is the custodian of the young heir but not the custodian of the older one?"
Imam (as) replied: "Yes, the executor should testify truthfully and must not conceal his testimony."

Furthermore, he wrote to Imam (as): "Is the testimony of the executor against the deceased regarding a debt, along with another just witness, acceptable?"
Imam (as) replied: "Yes, but only after an oath."
